metadata.title: Amazon To Pull Unauthorized Victoria's Secret Listings On Thanksgiving

content.text:
Amazon will remove Victoria's Secret listingsfrom third-party sellers on Amazon's marketplace on the Thanksgiving Day holiday, but will continue to allow authorized sellers to sell the Victoria's Secret brand.
The restriction,which the company posted on LinkedIn, directly affects several groups of Amazon advertisers -- including third-party resellers, competing brands, and Victoria's Secret's own first-partyadvertising team.
Third-party sellers have built entire businesses buying discounted name-brand goods at outlets or liquidation sales and reselling them on Amazon, and this move permanentlycloses that door for many household names, but some believe it is to protect brands against counterfeit and gray market sellers.
Although the policy primarily targets marketplace sellingprivileges, it will create immediate ripple effects across Amazon Ads such as Sponsored Products, Sponsored Brands, and Sponsored Display.
Ephraim Rosenberg, founder of Amazon Sellers Group(ASGTG), posted the notice. He supports marketplace compliance and seller advocacy. The terms were signed by Amazon Services were emailed to sellers.
"Victoria's Secret listings onAmazon.com will be restricted to sellers with the Brand Representative role starting November 26," Rosenberg wrote in a LinkedIn post. "Amazon says the brand distributes directly toconsumers rather than through wholesalers or third-party resellers."
Affected sellers of Victoria's Secret products are being advised to sell their remaining inventory before thedeadline. Victoria's Secret was already fairly restricted, but this makes the policy more explicit, he wrote.
The move appears to align with a wave of Brand Registry restrictions thatAmazon rolled out in late 2026, where several major brands were designated as "no longer eligible for third-party sellers" without an explicit brand-assigned role.
Based on reports, other brands include Nike, Adidas, Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Apple, Sony, Electronic Arts,L'Oréal, CeraVe, Estée Lauder Companies brands such as Clinique and MAC Cosmetics, Pacifica, LEGO, Starbucks, and more.
Amazon typically takes action like this becausethese brands typically sell direct to consumers and do not sell through wholesalers, distributors, or third-party reseller channels.
For example, Chanel does not sell products online throughits own website or through major retailers like Neiman Marcus, but prefers to sell its products straight to consumers through a brand representative at one of its boutiques.
Under Amazon BrandRegistry rules, the "Brand Representative" role is reserved for internal, first-party accounts directly employed or manually authorized by the trademark owner.
